chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A single dirham of usury (riba) is more severe than thirty acts of adultery, all of them with a close female relative, such as an aunt (paternal or maternal).

key_terms.بِذَاتِ مَحْرَمٍ: With a close female relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.رِبًا: Usury or interest, specifically referring to the prohibited increase in financial transactions
key_terms.زَنْيَةً: Adultery or fornication, referring to the act of unlawful sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: How does the severity of a small amount of usury compare to adultery in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts that a single dirham of usury is spiritually more severe than thirty acts of adultery with close female relatives (khala and 'amma), a comparison rooted in the specific legal status of these relatives as both mahram and non-permanent marriage partners. This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the gravity of riba by contrasting it with zina, highlighting how financial impurity disrupts the social and spiritual fabric of the community just as profoundly as sexual transgression.
